newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAD arm supports S.African health moves.
newsitem.headline: SAD arm supports S.African health moves.

text.p: Pharmacare, a division of South African Druggists Ltd, said on Monday it supported Health Minister Nkosazana Zuma's health reforms that aim to promote the substitution of branded drugs with generic alternatives.
Pharmacare, which exports generic drugs to 39 countries, said the moves were an effective way of ensuring adequate primary health care and reducing costs.
"The perception is that generics are of a lower quality than branded ehtical drugs. This is simply not true," Pharmacare chief executive Kobus Nel said in a statement.
Generic drugs are cheaper versions of branded drugs that have lost their patent protection.
The moves have angered some pharmaceutical manufacturers who say the moves deny patients' free choice in their medicine.

International pharmaceutical firms say the overall reform proposals, which also includes moves to limit the use of their fiercely protected brand names, could discourage foreign investment into the country.
